discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 180901
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
501 AM EDT Sun Oct 18 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- After a possible period of patchy frost tonight and maybe
  Monday night, lows trend warmer, away from frost potential.
  Highs also moderate to near or just above normal.

- Dry weather remains across the area through this week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 214 AM EDT Sun Oct 18 2026

Surface high pressure slowly slides eastward today from the southern 
Great Lakes and then a couple more surface high pressure systems 
pass by to the north of the Great Lakes Tuesday and Thursday. 
Meanwhile, mid level ridging continues to keep the area within a 
large scale area of subsidence quelling any large scale area of rain 
through this week and probably through next weekend. This is even as 
a cold front stalls around the area Monday night/Tuesday and another 
cold front moves through later Wednesday/Thursday AM time frame. 
These FROPAs will be dry FROPAs. Troughs attempt to make their way 
eastward but continue to run into the stout mid level ridge east of 
the Rockies through this work week. As such, various vort 
maxes/surface lows take a northeast trek from the Plains into the 
western Great Lakes/southcentral Canada area. Attempts by WAA 
to affect the area cause a slow warming trend through the 60s 
today and Monday, reaching the 70s for highs on Tuesday 
southwest of US-30 through this week. Daily lows look to trend 
warmer as well beyond this morning. There's a marginal chance 
for frost Monday morning with about 3 hours of 38 degree temps 
or less, especially south of US-24. However, another 
frost/freeze issuance will depend on if the growing season 
continues or if this morning's temps ended things. The area is 
fairly dry with MinRH values dipping into the 20s and 30s of 
percents today through Tuesday, but low level lapse rates aren't
as strong as they could be, and even more of a factor, wind 
gusts are below considerable thresholds. Future dry days are 
possible beyond Tuesday, but wind gusts don't look respectable 
at this time. It is also possible our forecast dew points are 
too high as currently constituted beyond Tuesday.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z MONDAY/... 
Issued at 500 AM EDT Sun Oct 18 2026

Dry and stable air mass will continue to promote VFR conditions
and clear skies. Return south-southwest flow on the backside of
sfc high pressure may support a few gusts up to 20 knots this 
afternoon at KSBN otherwise.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...Frost Advisory until 9 AM EDT /8 AM CDT/ this morning for 
     INZ005-012>015-020-022-103-104-203-204.
     Freeze Warning until 9 AM EDT this morning for INZ006>009-017-
     018-023>027-032>034-116-216.
OH...Freeze Warning until 9 AM EDT this morning for OHZ001-002-004-
     005-015-016-024-025.
MI...Frost Advisory until 9 AM EDT this morning for MIZ078>081-177-
     277.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Roller
AVIATION...Steinwedel

spc.text:
SPC AC 181230

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0730 AM CDT Sun Oct 18 2026

   Valid 181300Z - 191200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not forecast through tonight.

   ...Synopsis and Discussion...
   Even with east-northeasterly low-level flow persisting to the north
   of a remnant cold front, diurnal heating of a moist airmass will
   support sufficient instability for isolated to scattered
   thunderstorms across parts of south FL and the Keys today.
   Occasional lightning flashes may also occur with convection across
   parts of the Southwest ahead of a low-amplitude mid-level shortwave
   trough. Weak shear across south FL and limited moisture/instability
   over AZ/NM will hinder the potential for severe thunderstorms across
   both regions. Dry and/or stable conditions will preclude
   thunderstorms for the remainder of the CONUS through the period.

   ..Gleason/Kerr.. 10/18/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1630Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 180550

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1250 AM CDT Sun Oct 18 2026

   Valid 191200Z - 201200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not expected tomorrow (Monday).

   ...Synopsis...
   A mid-level cut-off low will continue to meander off of the East
   Coast while an upper trough amplifies over the western U.S. and an
   upper ridge dominates the central CONUS tomorrow (Monday). Surface
   high pressure and accompanying subsidence should limit thunderstorm
   development over most locales east of the Rockies. A couple of
   thunderstorms may develop over the FL Keys given adequate surface
   heating of a moist low-level airmass. A few thunderstorms may also
   occur over the Desert Southwest to the Four Corners, where cooler
   temperatures aloft with a mid-level impulse overspreads modest
   low-level moisture.

   ..Squitieri.. 10/18/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 180729

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0229 AM CDT Sun Oct 18 2026

   Valid 201200Z - 211200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe thunderstorms are expected on Tuesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper trough will amplify while progressing into the Interior
   West on Tuesday. As this occurs, deep-layer ascent and cooler
   temperatures aloft will encourage at least isolated thunderstorm
   development over multiple locales. Preceding the main upper trough,
   a 500 mb wind maximum accompanying multiple low-amplitude impulses
   will overspread low-level moisture over the Desert Southwest, as
   well as portions of the Great Basin, resulting in thunderstorms by
   Tuesday afternoon. By later Tuesday night into Wednesday morning,
   deep-layer ascent associated with the approach of the primary upper
   trough will overspread parts of CA. Cooler temperatures aloft will
   overspread a marine boundary layer, encouraging lightning flashes
   along the CA shoreline late in the period.

   ..Squitieri.. 10/18/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
